cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Kafka is a distributed, durable, append-only log. Unlike a queue, consuming a message does not remove it: each consumer tracks its own offset, so many consumer groups can read and replay the same stream independently.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Topics split into partitions across brokers. Ordering is guaranteed per partition only, so use a key like order ID. Each partition goes to one consumer per group; extra consumers sit idle. Retention is time or size based. Partitions replicate with a leader and ISR; use acks=all with idempotent producers.

questions.a: Only within one partition. Use the same key for an entity so its events land in one partition.

questions.q: What happens with more consumers than partitions in a group?
questions.a: The extra consumers sit idle; each partition goes to exactly one consumer in the group.
The in-sync replicas: followers caught up closely enough to take over if the leader fails.
